headline: Single-cell atlases map mouse cardiac regeneration, aging splicing and strain variation
label: Single Cell Mouse Transcriptome Atlases
summary: Large single-nucleus atlases of mouse tissues now allow expression variation and splicing programs to be compared across strains, ages and species.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of single-cell transcriptomic data in mouse as a reusable resource for comparative analysis. MCAREDB consolidates mouse scRNA-seq datasets of neonatal versus adult cardiac regeneration into a freely accessible web database with cell-type expression information. The aging study applies LeafletFA, a probabilistic model, to scRNA-seq from mouse and human atlases to identify aging-associated alternative splicing programs conserved between the two species. The eight-tissue snRNA-seq atlas profiles 5.2 million nuclei and 106 cell types across eight Collaborative Cross founder strains, quantifying global and local expression variation. What is new is the extension of single-cell comparisons beyond cell-type-level analysis to isoform-level splicing and to genetic background. The items differ in data type and purpose, so the shared element is methodological and resource-oriented rather than a common mechanism.
